newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Japan PM sacrifices anniversary to diplomacy.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM sacrifices anniversary to diplomacy.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Monday he had sacrificed most of his wedding anniversary to the demands of diplomacy.
But he still managed to celebrate by sharing a bottle of Australian wine with his wife Kumiko on the flight from the United States, he said.
Hashimoto, who arrived in Australia earlier in the day for a visit after his Friday meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton, mentioned his domestic sacrifice in a speech on Japan-Australia ties.
"After we took off from Honolulu, we drank a bottle of Australian wine together," Hashimoto said.
"I'm sure it was Australian wine, but I got drunk, so I forgot the label," Hashimoto joked.

Hashimoto said he had given Kumiko an Australian black opal to make up for missing nearly all of their anniversary on Sunday because of the travel schedule, which kept the couple in flight for some 20 hours between Washington and Sydney.
"It's very elegant, but it's expensive," he said of his wife's present, noting it cost four times the price of the cufflinks he bought for himself.

Hashimoto also joked that Australia's black opal exports could become a problem for the trade balance between Japan and Australia -- one of the few nations with which Tokyo runs a deficit -- since he was likely to have to buy similar gems for other family members.
